links.outcome: LLM specialty competitiveness and surgical recommendations varying with synthetic applicant race and gender
links.effect: Male applicants rated more competitive than female (P<0.0001); Black and Hispanic less competitive than White (P=0.0019, 0.0108); male surgical recommendation OR 10.23; Black and Hispanic females needed 95 and 88 extra Step 2 points vs 56 for White females.
links.quote: Compensatory scoring revealed that White female applicants needed 56 additional Step 2 Clinical Knowledge points to match perceived competitiveness, whereas Black and Hispanic female applicants required 95 and 88 additional points, respectively.

screen.reason: Empirical audit testing racial and gender bias of an LLM used for medical student career advising on synthetic profiles; it evaluates model bias but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
